title: Supersymmetry and Entanglement in the Generalized Dirac Oscillator
authors: H. P. Laba, V. M. Tkachuk
abstract: The supersymmetric properties of the generalized Dirac oscillator allow us to determine the entanglement entropy between the spin and the continuous variable in a purely algebraic manner. The entanglement has a relativistic origin and disappears in the nonrelativistic limit. The entanglement entropy attains its maximal value in the limit of infinite energy.
summary: This paper analyzes the entanglement entropy in the generalized Dirac oscillator by leveraging the mathematical structure provided by Supersymmetry. It demonstrates that the entanglement vanishes in the nonrelativistic limit, confirming its purely relativistic origin. The findings offer a systematic theoretical tool connecting symmetry properties to quantifiable measures of quantum correlation.
main_problem: The study systematically investigates the interplay between supersymmetry (SUSY) and quantum entanglement within generalized Dirac oscillator systems.
main_result: The entanglement entropy is found to be zero in both the ground state and the nonrelativistic limit, suggesting that entanglement has a purely relativistic origin. Furthermore, it attains its maximum value in the infinite energy limit.
method: The analysis employs Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanics (SUSY QM) techniques to relate the spin degree of freedom to the continuous variable via SUSY partner eigenstates ($	ilde{\phi}, 	ilde{\chi}$). Entanglement entropy is calculated by analyzing the reduced density matrix derived from the state vector.
model_or_system: The physical model is the Generalized Dirac Oscillator, a relativistic quantum system whose Hamiltonian structure allows for supersymmetric decomposition. The analysis focuses on its eigenstates and their coupling between spin and spatial components.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy ($S$), Overlap integral ($Z$), Energy eigenvalues ($E$).
important_parameters: Relativistic energy $E$, mass $m$, Superpotential function $W(x)$, and the parameter $\epsilon = (E/c)^2 - m^2c^2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the framework of SUSY QM, utilizing specific transformations ($\hat{B}, \hat{B}^+$) to relate the components.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the generalized Dirac oscillator Hamiltonian, decomposes it using SUSY partners, calculates the entanglement entropy based on the resulting state coefficients and overlap integral $Z$, and analyzes the limits (ground state, nonrelativistic limit) to derive physical conclusions.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical link between fundamental symmetries (SUSY) and quantum information measures (entanglement), which is highly relevant for understanding entanglement generation in relativistic or structured quantum systems.
